newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 11.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The balance sum in the Czech National Bank on June 30 was 19.304 billion crowns more than 10 years ago and amounted to 644.945 billion crowns.

- The Finance Ministry yesterday unblocked accounts with shares of funds administered by A-Invest, which was under forced administration until June. Three funds will be administered by Expandia Finance.
- One of the world's largest tractor makers, Zetor, should join forces with Motokov International if the cabinet approves a proposal for this.

- Part of a business plan which the general director of Czech Railways will present to the administrative council today is to lay off 17,000 people over the next three years. MLADA FRONTA DNES - Water levels are going down in northern Moravia, but some of it is moving south and flooding central and southern Moravia. Floods surrounded Otrakovice yesterday, and about one third of the country is still underwater.

- The cabinet has decided that it will request the National Property Fund to free up three billion crowns from revenue from small privatisations and it will issue government bonds of five billion crowns to help cover damages caused by the floods.
- The official number of deaths due to floods in Moravia increased yesterday to 23 people.

- Extensive floods, which have slowed the operations of many businesses are also taking their toll on the stock exchange and the crown. Shares of construction companies rose yesterday, while shares of the companies affected declined. The crown weakened.
- According to spokesman Tomas Kopriva, Prvni Investicni will appeal against the Finance Ministry's decision to issue it the highest fine possible -- 10 million crowns.

- Ceska Sporitelna and Universal Banka announced changes in interest rates yesterday. From Monday, Sporitelna will decrease its interest rate for savings accounts to 20 percent and increase rates for short-term and medium-term accounts of more than one month.

- A Prague court ruled to block the accounts of the investment fund AGB II, which should have a general meeting today and was recently placed under forced administration. PRAVO - For the first half of this year, Tatra Koprivnice posted turnover of more than 5.5 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of 77 percent.
- Stock Plzen wants to buy the state's 89-percent stake in Jan Becher-Karlovarska Becherovka, for which the Finance Ministry announced a multi-criteria tender.
- Skoda Auto, which stopped production of Felicia automobiles on Wednesday because it lacked supplies of autoparts from factories in the flood-stricken region of Moravia, will renew production today.
- On Sunday, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will meet with President Vaclav Havel and Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec in Prague.
- Beginning today, Ceska Posta will accept packages with material help for residents of regions affected by floods at no charge.

- The cabinet decided on Thursday to send 5,000 soldiers to help police in flooded areas. LIDOVE NOVINY - Severoceska Energetika received assurance of the money it is owed by Czech Railways and is no longer threatening to cut off the railways' electricity.
- The largest Czech paper and cellulose maker, Sepap, based in Steti, changed its name to AssiDoman Sepap a.s.
- Parliament stripped Republican Josef Krejsa of his immunity yesterday and proposed criminal prosecution for articles with an anti-gypsy theme printed in the magazine Republika.
